title: sync --to-store has two warning surfaces and neither reports a COMMITTED attachment whose bytes differ from canon: one never examines attachments, the other examines git state instead of content, so the divergence enters canon in silence
body:
**NEITHER OF THIS VERB'S TWO WARNING SURFACES REPORTS AN ATTACHMENT WHOSE COMMITTED BYTES DIFFER FROM CANON. One does not examine attachments at all; the other examines git state instead of content. So a clean, committed, diverged attachment is ingested into canon in silence, and the run says nothing was overwritten.**

**AMENDED 2026-09-05 BY THE REPORTER, on a second firing from another node that refuted the original headline. What was struck is named so a reader can tell a withdrawal from an omission.**

## What I filed first, and why it did not survive

The original said the warning surface excludes attachments outright. **That is too strong and a live firing disproves it.** Lamplight's `ic` node edited one work package in `ST0315.json`, ran `sync --to-store`, and got a real attachment warning naming a file:

```
warning: 1 attachment(s) carry bytes no commit contains, and this run takes them into canon:
  intent/st/ST0359/workspace-status.md: edited in the working tree and not staged
  commit them first if canon should name bytes a reader can obtain -- this run does not refuse, and the commit gate will
```

The surface exists, it is well written, and it fired. **My error was concluding from one silent run that the check was absent, when what I had established was that THAT check was silent -- and I never grepped for a second emitter.** A null result is evidence about the search.

## What survives, sharpened by the refutation

There are **two** warning surfaces on this path and they answer different questions:

- **`render.rs:1031` -- the OVERWRITES list.** Computed by `facade.rs:3610 sync_overwrite`, comparing `store.load_canon()` against `ingest::read(&self.project)`. `ingest::read` (`ingest.rs:258`) walks the canon JSON and the opaque-attachment sidecars; **it has no call to `collect_attachments_into`** (`ingest.rs:462`), which is what the write path uses at `facade.rs:3490` from `sync_from_disk` (`facade.rs:3450`) to carry disk attachment text into canon. So this list cannot name an attachment divergence.
- **`render.rs:1047` / `:1054` -- the uncommitted-attachment warning.** `sync_uncommitted` classifies each attachment path as `NotInIndex::Modified` ("tracked, and the working tree differs from what is staged") or `NotInIndex::Untracked` (`sync.rs:833-844`). **It is a git-cleanliness check, not a divergence check.**

**The gap is their intersection, and it is not a corner case.** An attachment that is committed and clean is neither `Modified` nor `Untracked`, so the second surface is silent -- `Some(found) if found.is_empty() => {}` at `render.rs:1051` prints nothing at all. And an attachment is invisible to the first surface by construction. **A committed attachment whose bytes differ from what canon holds is therefore reported by neither, and ingested by the write.**

## Two measurements, the same verb, opposite halves of the gap

**1. Committed and diverged -- SILENT. Lamplight ST0359, 2026-09-05.** `workspace-status.md` on disk `6622B / 00b3a162` (committed at Lamplight `4723bc6f4`, tree clean); store, worktree extract and HEAD extract all `6589B / 3b2cf840`. Store and extract agree, so the OVERWRITES list is empty and correct. Disk is clean, so the uncommitted warning is empty and correct. Output in full:

```
note: no thread the store already holds differs on disk, so this restore overwrites nothing (a thread the extract has and the store does not is an ADD and is not examined here)
ok: store rewritten from the canon extract, 1 thread(s); nothing the store already held was overwritten
```

rc 0, no warning of any kind, and both artefacts moved: `intent.db` `97addf6c` -> `362503ca`, `ST0359.json` `34bc6a18` -> `034fd8ba`. After the run, disk, store and worktree extract all read `6622B / 00b3a162`. **The 33 bytes came from a markdown file that neither check had read.**

**2. Uncommitted -- WARNED, correctly, and still worth recording.** `ic`'s firing above, on a thread they had not touched: the run replaced the store across all 358 threads and took dc's unstaged `workspace-status.md` into canon at `6622 -> 8531B`, rewriting the rendered view. Nothing was lost -- the bytes were dc's own newer content, since committed at Lamplight `41e87f3a7`.

## Three things the second firing shows that the first could not

- **The two surfaces have different populations and only one of them says so.** The OVERWRITES list named exactly one thread, `ST0315`, the reporter's own. The run rewrote 358 and ingested an attachment from `ST0359`, a thread that list does not mention. A reader has no way to tell from the output that the first list is not the scope of the act.
- **The warning names a COUNT and a PATH, never an owner.** "1 attachment(s)" tells you something happened and not to whom, so the node that must act on it -- dc -- is exactly the node the message cannot reach. It reached them because `ic` read a fifteen-line tail and sent a message by hand.
- **dc's framing, which is the sharpest of the three:** this is a warning that IS emitted, correctly, into a channel whose normal use discards it. Not absent, not wrong -- reliably unread. A run piped through a grep for `ok:` shows a clean success.

## Why it matters beyond wording

`design.md`, `impl.md` and `tasks.md` are ruled authored prose carried as attachments (Lamplight `bd7ee1ab3`), so this is the normal shape of an attachment. In a tree several nodes commit to, a node syncing its own thread ingests whatever any other node has left on disk for any thread in scope. **Case 2 is the loud version of that and case 1 is the quiet one**, and the quiet one is the version that ships.

**It also defeats the mitigation the reporting estate had standing for this class.** The advice is *diff the artifact, never the rc* -- but the artifact a careful operator reaches for first is the extract, and in case 1 the extract is one of the two sides that already agreed. A mitigation is only outside a blind spot if you can say what the blind spot is.

## What is NOT claimed

That either check is wrong at what it does. `sync_overwrite` answers truthfully about the population it walks, the uncommitted warning answers truthfully about the index, and ingesting the disk attachment is `collect_attachments_into`'s stated job under the ruling that an attachment divergence means the disk wins. **The defect is that no surface answers the question an operator running a restore is actually asking: what is about to change.**

## Suggested shape, not a design

Give the attachment check a **content** predicate alongside its git predicate: compare each attachment's disk bytes against the canon the store holds, and name a divergence the way a differing thread is already named (`ST0359: attachment workspace-status.md differs on disk`). That covers both cases with one line and makes the committed-and-diverged case the same shape as the uncommitted one. If the comparison is too expensive on the warning path, the honest fallback is the remedy `0111` strand 2 already established: say in the message what was NOT examined, the way the ADD is now named.

**A regression test should assert the INVARIANT, with both arms.** With store and extract identical and one COMMITTED attachment's markdown differing on disk, a run that changes canon must not report that nothing was overwritten. Its control is the other arm -- an attachment identical on disk must still produce the quiet message -- without which the test is satisfied by a binary that warns unconditionally.

## Related

`0111` -- same verb, same family. Its strand 1 (the contradictory "overwrites nothing" plus "store replaced") is FIXED at `557d220d` and the fixed wording is what both firings above printed. Its strand 2 named the ADD blind spot in the message text; this is a second blind spot in the same sentence's neighbourhood. `0082` is the other direction (`--to-disk` not materialising a new attachment).
